title: Female borrowers who use character-based descriptors like 'dedication' or 'resilience' may fund faster.
Female borrowers who include direct thank you notes to lenders may fund more slowly.
Qualitative personal identifiers (like names) may accelerate funding for women, while quantitative demographic data (like marital status) may decelerate it.
Pitches with a higher word count or greater overall length tend to fund more slowly for both male and female borrowers.
Pitches from women that explicitly state the borrower's level of education tend to accelerate funding speed.
Female borrowers who provide detailed descriptions of their local environment or business operations fund more slowly.
Mentioning a lack of collateral may accelerate funding speed for female borrowers.
Pitches from women highlighting skill development or asset acquisition accelerate funding, whereas listing specific technical inputs like seeds or fertilizers decelerates it.
Female borrowers who mention the loan amount in local currency may fund more slowly.
Pitches that highlight owning assets or a lack of rental obligations accelerate funding for both men and women.
Mentioning specific institutional or brand names predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Mentioning benefits for children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention their general family structure fund faster.
Female borrowers who include specific demographic details fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention a history of previous loan repayments fund faster.
